title: Personal Checking: new-account period, check hold and mobile deposit limits by tier
content:
## Scope

This reference covers the deposit-side figures of each Personal Checking tier: the new-account period, the business day on which a check deposited to a new account posts, and the mobile deposit limits.

## New-account period and check hold

| Tier | New-account period: calendar days after the opening date during which new-account treatment applies to holds and disputes | Check deposited during the new-account period posts and becomes available on this business day after deposit |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 30 | 5 |
| Student Checking | 30 | 5 |
| Everyday Checking | 30 | 5 |
| Interest Checking | 30 | 5 |
| Premier Checking | 30 | 5 |
| Private Client Checking | 30 | 5 |

## Mobile deposit limits

| Tier | Most check value deposited through mobile deposit per calendar day (USD) | Most check value deposited through mobile deposit in any rolling 30 calendar days (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 1500.00 | 5000.00 |
| Student Checking | 1000.00 | 3000.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 3500.00 | 10000.00 |
| Interest Checking | 5000.00 | 15000.00 |
| Premier Checking | 10000.00 | 30000.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 25000.00 | 75000.00 |

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Does the new-account period differ by tier?**
A: No. It is 30 calendar days after the opening date on every tier, and a check deposited while the account has been open fewer than that many days posts on the 5th business day after deposit.

**Q: Which tier has the lowest mobile deposit limits?**
A: Student Checking, at 1000.00 USD per calendar day and 3000.00 USD in any rolling 30 calendar days.

**Hypothetical case**: an Everyday Checking owner has already deposited 9000.00 USD through mobile deposit in the rolling 30 calendar days. The 30-day figure for that tier is 10000.00 USD, so 1000.00 USD of room remains in that window, subject also to the daily figure of 3500.00 USD.
